correctness.rationale: The lower support bound is exact by the Euclidean triangle inequality applied to incidence edge vectors; independent coordinate-sign symmetries plus axis caps and uniqueness give the global John ellipsoid. Connectedness and equality in that triangle inequality give exactly 2n John contacts. Cauchy–Schwarz gives a universal outer inclusion. Under connected bipartiteness, all equal-edge-norm normals have partwise uniform magnitudes, and the resulting complete contact arcs are explicitly parametrized. Biregularity yields an exact 2^n signed isotropic contact design; the trace/determinant argument proves unique global Löwner minimality against all translated or rotated ellipsoids. Arc incidence yields K_{2^p,2^q} and its Betti number. A standalone current-package checker successfully evaluated 8,500 supports, 1,348 contacts, and 193 covariance entries; it is only corroborative.

value.rationale: The graph-degree formula determines the entire John ellipsoid for every no-isolate graph, not merely an inradius; the complementary Löwner theorem classifies a natural infinite family of sparse and nonregular discotopes, including all rectangular complete bipartite graphs and stars. The full outer contact locus has an exponentially growing, exactly prescribed complete-bipartite topology independent of the graph edges beyond biregularity; this is geometric information not supplied by the scalar radius or by the previously treated regular case. Exact axis ratios and contact topology offer reproducible benchmarks for nonpolyhedral zonoids.
